title: A-scalar-CAR-pair-transit-v2 (the scalar channel)
summary: One object or none on every seam and on every wedge, a wedge being two seams at one port. An object hops between a seam and a wedge, which sit at the two opposite levels +m and -m.

services.quantity: loop instruments, reference ramps, pulses and pointers

native_cell.detail: the labelling is the fixed cell

locality.detail: every coupling joins incident registers of one cell

rotations.detail: commutes with the sixty rotations of the cell (largest defect 0.0e+00)

federation.detail: builds on cell (the scalar channel is written on one cell)

parameters.detail: declared parameter descriptions pass provenance and forbidden-input checks

one-law.requirement: Every premise assigned to the law is fulfilled by one unchanged law on one process.

einstein-together.requirement: The stress that observers infer from modular flow is the stress carried by the excitations that propagate and interact under the law.

matter-together.requirement: Gauge currents act on those excitations through the law's operations; detector, generator, clock and currents refer to the same object.

patch-measurement.requirement: Finite patches measure both the current response and the stress of one bound excitation with their own clocks and records.

relativistic-matter.requirement: The rest energy and the inertia of every bound excitation follow one dictionary.

premises.name: confluent terminating repair contract
premises.statement: Declared repair moves close every covered local mismatch, overlapping moves complete to a common local diamond on the quotient, and every accepted nontrivial aggregate transaction strictly lowers one declared well-founded exact measure, so repair reduction terminates and normal endpoints from sources with equal protected observation agree exactly when the observation identifies consistent states. The contract is declared through the rows repair_completeness, local_diamond, and strict_well_founded_transactional_descent in claims/assumption_dictionary.md; the endpoint-uniqueness characterization is machine-checked in Lean/ObservableNormalForms/ObservableNormalForms/ObserverConfluence.lean.

premises.name: algebra-state representation of public records
premises.statement: Public records are represented as the span of the mutually orthogonal projectors of a projective partition inside a finite complex matrix star algebra, with states read through the trace pairing and record events using that declared algebraic readout surface. The representation is packaged in Lean/EventAlgebra/PublicRecordAlgebra.lean and declared as declared_record_surface in claims/assumption_dictionary.md.
premises.note: Loop instruments and the complete law of two pointers are finite instruments with their back-action; the representation of the records is supplied with them.

premises.name: operational effect additivity
premises.statement: A public frame valuation is additive on every required coexistent effect sum, v(A + B) = v(A) + v(B) whenever A + B remains an effect, across measurement contexts. With this additivity the finite Busch-Gleason theorem in Lean/EventAlgebra/FiniteBuschGleason.lean forces the Born trace form; the same module carries the countermodel in which positivity, per-context normalisation, and continuity hold while cross-context additivity fails, and the row source_produced_public_effect_algebra_deferred in claims/assumption_dictionary.md records that the retained finite unsharp web admits a transverse cubic non-Born valuation.

premises.name: declared phase-sensitive effect
premises.statement: The exact matrix I/2 - (2*sqrt(3)/3)*i*(QP - PQ), equal to the Pauli-Y plus projector, is one declared phase-sensitive effect. Together with the two committed real effects it completes fixed-trace two-by-two tomography. This declaration supplies an effect only, not a quantum operation or instrument; CP outcome maps, a trace-preserving summed channel, preparation, readback, and provenance are separate premises.

premises.name: counting path reference
premises.statement: The path-space reference is a supplied initial law times the uniform-step counting weight; among row-stochastic kernels this normal form is characterized by invariance under independent relabeling of transition targets at fixed source, by row-constant weight, or by constant log-transition step action, and the formalized Axiom 3 takes the reference as an input, so no theorem selects the counting reference or the trivial datum whose conditional resampling realizes it. The reference is formalized in Lean/InformationProjection/LogTransitionAction.lean; Lean/InformationProjection/ReferenceNormalForm.lean proves the characterization, and Lean/InformationProjection/SourceReferenceSelection.lean proves the conditional counting-reference realization together with the rescaling and initial-law non-uniqueness controls.

premises.name: real Legendre enrichment
premises.statement: The finite source law fixes its four-corner log-transition action and a bilinear real extension that is affine in the velocity slot; adding (a/2)*y*(y - 1) for any a > 0 changes no realized source history and yields strictly convex Legendre-Hamilton systems that differ between values of a. Selecting one real velocity curvature is therefore a representation choice beyond the realized-history law, proved as an explicit-witness nonidentifiability on the committed chain literals in Lean/Variational/RealizedHistoryLegendreNoGo.lean with the bridge itself in Lean/Variational/LegendreBridge.lean; finer alphabets, refinement limits, and other source data are untested by it.

premises.name: declared repair law: common faithful reference and repaired-visible fibre
premises.statement: One common faithful reference serves both Axiom 3 instantiations, and the transition feasible set is the fibre of the complete repaired visible datum of the active collar; on these two declared inputs the state projection selects the Gibbs exponential family and the transition projection selects weighted conditional resampling from the same reference, which yields the exact four-law package. The pair is declared through the row complete_repaired_visible_datum_fibre in claims/assumption_dictionary.md and consumed by Lean/Thermodynamics/FiniteConditionalRepair.lean; the B12 obstruction (code/thermodynamics/common_reference_obstruction/) and the B20 random-scan preflight (code/b20_random_scan/) prove that the pinned source run and its certified random-scan grammar do not supply the pair.

premises.name: refinement-uniform low-temperature control
premises.statement: A declared indexed family carries one uniform low-temperature tail bound strong enough to drive the off-minimum Gibbs mass, and where claimed the entropy excess, to zero with one inverse-temperature threshold across the family. The original sufficient member uses a uniformly positive energy gap plus a uniform finite cardinality bound to obtain cardBound * exp(-beta * gapBound); its maps preserve minima but do not supply the later functorial and cofinal structure. The coherent-envelope route adds directed functorial data, and the ambient-cofinal route adds a nonterminal regulator embedding plus strict carrier growth on one supplied spectral-tail family. Neither route is asserted to be necessary for every growing regulator tower. A direct density-of-states or excited-to-ground degeneracy-ratio bound remains an allowed alternative.

premises.name: equal-face-weight and barycentric one-third port-dual rules
premises.statement: The port-dual measure places equal normalized weights on the twenty faces of the oriented carrier, and each face's weight is shared barycentrically, one third to each incident port, giving the normalized port-dual weight 1/12. The rules are declared in code/b14_jacobi/port_dual_metric_selector.certificate.json (declared_rules.face_weighting and declared_rules.vertex_share), with the measure pinned by the committed theorem in Lean/Screen/PrimitivePortDualMeasure.lean.

Both rules are declared in code/b14_jacobi/port_dual_metric_selector.certificate.json (declared_rules.measure_to_metric and declared_rules.repair_rule) and in the row carrier_induced_invariant_metric_class_and_nearest_point_rule of claims/assumption_dictionary.md; neither is source-derived.

premises.name: compact-Lie classification inputs
premises.statement: Three Lie-theory facts enter the gauge classification as declared classical inputs: the direct-sum splitting L = Z(L) + [L, L] of a compact Lie algebra into invariant submodules, surjectivity of the exponential map on compact connected groups, and the classification of compact simple Lie algebras through its dimension list. The cited modules declare the remaining Lie-theoretic bridge steps of the classification (centre rationality through the torus/cocharacter step, the su(2)^4 fixed-space exclusion, and the reductive-decomposition boundary bundle) as classical inputs subsumed under this row. They are marked as inputs in Lean/Screen/A5OPH.lean and Lean/Screen/TrichotomyCases.lean and cited by paper/deriving_standard_model_gauge_structure_from_observer_overlap_consistency.tex.

premises.name: matter candidate grammar
premises.statement: A matter candidate is a pair (S, M): S a stratum of the classified compact locus of the fourteen-parameter equivariant Jacobi variety on the twelve-port carrier, and M a nonempty Z/2-graded finite-dimensional complex module of the complexified semisimple bracket at S with zero abelian charges and total dimension at most twelve, counted up to graded isomorphism and the global parity flip. The grammar, budget, observables, and decision rule are frozen before any comparison in code/b15_matter_freeze/matter_class_freeze_v1.json; the exterior selection boundary is recorded as exterior_Higgs_matter_selection in claims/assumption_dictionary.md.

premises.name: Koide balance premise
premises.statement: For a positive-chamber face circulant with square-root masses sqrt(m_k) = sqrt(s)*(a + 2*rho*cos(delta + 2*pi*k/3)), the balance premise rho/a = 1/sqrt(2) makes the signed Koide quotient equal 2/3 exactly. premises.statement: The hadronic vacuum-polarization and spectral input is a pinned empirical payload built from the e+e- hadronic compilation registered in code/particles/hadron/empirical_ee_hadrons_sources.yaml (KNT19, arXiv:1911.00367, per docs/policies/HADRON.md), consumed by the Ward-projected hadron lane and the alpha(m_Z) anchor transport as a flagged import. premises.name: clock and energy calibration anchors
premises.statement: Internal modular charge, energy gaps, and repair-step order carry no laboratory units. PR-15 is the empirical attachment to declared measured clock and energy standards, including conversion into laboratory or SI units. It is separate from the source-side independent_physical_scale_receipt in claims/assumption_dictionary.md: that structural receipt asks two internally generated readouts to remove positive-rescaling freedom before any empirical unit conversion, and it is not part of this import row. The four-law claim in claims/claim_registry.yaml records laboratory energy and clock calibration as a named empirical input shared by the thermodynamics and constants lanes.

premises.name: source-causal continuum and stable-causality certificate
premises.statement: Promotion of the source-derived finite event order and exact one-plus-three Lorentz carrier to a physical continuum requires one source-selected refinement family with physical event and link identification, injective two-way order-cone-faithful placements, compatible transport of order and source directions, dense and isotropic physical link directions on the source two-sphere, calibrated event count to spacetime volume, independent dimension, manifoldlikeness, interval-height, and stable-topology tests, a unique distinguishing Lorentzian limit, and convergent curvature estimators. Stable causality or global hyperbolicity remains an additional global condition wherever a downstream theorem invokes it. The finite carrier theorem supplies none of these continuum or physical-identification clauses.

premises.name: proposed fundamental numerical parameters P and N
premises.statement: P and N are the two proposed fundamental free numerical parameters of the program. Measured calibration anchors, fitted inputs, comparison targets, and empirical transport payloads are separate numerical empirical inputs and remain flagged as such; other quantities are derived or imported mathematics. The screen-grain proposal P = phi + sqrt(pi)/A_T(P) has an interval-certified fixed point (docs/AXIOM_REFERENCE.md, certified under code/P_derivation/), and the direct capacity proposal N = log M_0(U_N), declared as declared_capacity_map in claims/assumption_dictionary.md, is not evaluable on the incomplete source antecedent.

premises.name: spherically symmetric radial readout
premises.statement: A source distribution on the committed three-dimensional completion carrier is read through one radial strength profile: the flux through a shell depends on the shell radius alone. The premise enters as the strength field of RadialFluxData in Lean/Geometry/InverseSquareShellLaw.lean and is a symmetry declaration; no source theorem produces it.

Under it the inverse-square law is forced with the exponent supplied by the carrier dimension; no source theorem produces the normalization itself.

The committed record derives the spatial generator; the second-order evolution shape enters as this declaration and no source theorem produces it. The package is a theorem on the finite thermodynamic model and a declared supply beyond it.

premises.statement: An Einstein-admissible tower exists with protected boundary fibre, typed common-domain readouts, and refinement naturality; the strict dependency manifest validates; the discrete chart is connected in the symmetric step closure; the vacuum reference fixes the metric residue at the chart base; and the coupling carries the independent scale identification kappa = 8*pi*G_N.

premises.name: layered shell-cardinality law
premises.statement: The layered readout graph has exactly shellCoeff * n^2 outward boundary edges at shell n for every positive layer index n up to a declared resolution depth. The premise enters as the shellCard field of LayeredFluxData in Lean/Screen/LayeredDiscreteGauss.lean; no source theorem produces it. The committed 20 * n^2 faceCount in Lean/Screen/DiscreteRefinement.lean is a subdivision count on one fixed screen; identifying subdivision frequency with radial layer distance is exactly the open step, so the count is declared rather than derived. The depth truncation is forced: unbounded_shellCard_forces_zero proves an n^2 law imposed at every positive layer collapses the coefficient to zero on any finite carrier.

The premise enters as the equidistributed field of LayeredFluxData in Lean/Screen/LayeredDiscreteGauss.lean and is the discrete counterpart of the spherically symmetric radial readout premise (PR-18); no source theorem produces it.

The premise enters as the steadyGauss and sourceSupport fields of LayeredFluxData in Lean/Screen/LayeredDiscreteGauss.lean. The depth truncation is forced: steady_total_source_eq_zero proves a steady drained source on the whole closed finite carrier has zero total load, so layers beyond depth absorb the flux in place of spatial infinity. On the fixed twelve-port carrier the corresponding identity is a theorem: steady_witness_regionFlux_eq_source derives it from the committed regional continuity law.

For the support-disjoint pair (86, 247) the split is backed by the kernel-checked support disjointness theorem supports_disjoint; the split itself is declared, and the designated pair (86, 88) has overlapping supports with no disjointness receipt.

premises.name: same-source loop-to-kernel identity
premises.statement: The carrier loop classes realized by the source are the six-axis screen gluing classes of Lean/Screen/Z6Exact.lean, and their image under the committed intertwiner sixAxisToKernel of Lean/Screen/Z6Descent.lean (axis generator to the kernel generator (omega_3 I_3, -I_2, e^{i pi/3}), antipodal sign reversal to conjugation, injective with image exactly the tensor-action kernel) generates the full Z6 tensor-action kernel of Lean/Screen/TraceBalancedKernel.lean. The corresponding maximal faithful tensor-action image is S(U(3) x U(2)), equivalently (SU(3) x SU(2) x U(1))/Z6. The realized local weights descend through all four admissible quotients (Z6Descent.four_admissible_global_forms), so the same-source loop-to-kernel identity is one necessary clause toward selecting the physical quotient; it does not select that quotient without PR-46. The intertwiner itself is a proved receipt, and the premise is the same-source physical identification of its domain.

premises.name: family band-selection rules: single complete faithful band and operational cost order
premises.statement: The family multiplicity object is a single complete spectral band of the twelve-port adjacency realized inside the screen coefficient space: candidates carrying a source-visible proper splitting projector are excluded (the single-complete-object clause), bands whose rotation action has nontrivial kernel are excluded (the faithfulness clause), and the complex dimension lies in the pinned physical window [3, 5]. Admissible candidates are compared by the operational Laplacian seam cost per unit norm over Z[sqrt5], and the unique strict minimizer is selected. On the committed carrier the admissible candidates are the 3, 3', and 5 bands with exact costs 5 - sqrt5 < 6 < 5 + sqrt5, so the rules select the rank-three band (Lean/Screen/A5FamilyBand.lean, family_band_selected); over all four bands the minimizer is the trivial band at cost zero (trivial_band_without_faithfulness). On this finite table faithfulness and the [3, 5] window each exclude that same trivial entry: removing either condition while retaining the other changes no admissible candidate. The all-band control drops both exclusions; it does not show that either clause is separately necessary when the other is retained. The clauses are declared in code/a5_closure/family_band_attachment_certificate.py and its reference manifest.

The finite Stone-converse receipt then represents that supplied flow by conjugation with a time-independent self-adjoint generator, unique up to an additive real scalar. The premise supplies neither a source-selected evolution nor a physical clock.

These data yield exact algebraic no-signalling and dependency-cone identities but do not identify spacelike physical regions, a laboratory channel, or a source-selected factorization.

The finite Euler-Lagrange, Legendre-Hamilton, and Noether receipts are conditional on these data and are stated for fixed-endpoint interior-junction variations; the observer source does not select them.

The finite kernel, six-axis intertwiner, and four-quotient menu do not supply those identifications.

The exterior table and central-weight arithmetic identify a compatible candidate but do not select its physical existence or dynamics.

The exterior grammar records compatible invariant lines. The exact non-identifiability receipt holds both frames fixed and frees the two eigenvalue moduli, while matrices, textures, and phases are absent from the registered one-generation grammar.

premises.statement: The A5-invariant screen-load line and the electroweak scalar order-unit line are identified by one refinement-natural positive unital readout, and that same typed load is attached to the global capacity action used by the conditional N closure. The current branch certificate explicitly leaves the common-load identification and inherited screen-electroweak bridge premises open.

premises.statement: The source-derived finite informational order, the constructed ambient Lorentz target, and source-selected event placements are jointly identified with one observer-produced effective physical spacetime. This identification requires physical causal faithfulness of the order, a faithful embedding, a calibrated event-counting or replacement measure for spacetime volume, manifoldlikeness, independent recovery of intrinsic dimension and topology, compatible rods and operational clocks, stability across a physical continuum family, uniqueness of the limit, and convergence of metric, curvature, and stress data. The legacy EventGermAtlas remains an optional algebraic soldering adapter and is neither an input to nor the active route for this attachment. The existing algebraic geometry, provenance, placement, and finite-net modules explicitly do not construct the joint physical identification.

premises.statement: A named branch-indexed finite-carrier propagation action is identified with a physical photon or other declared field sector, a coherent frame and boost law, a calibrated clock and length scale, a cofinal gluing or continuum domain, and an operational wave-packet readout with nuisance and comparison semantics. The primitive-port rank-six and seam-current rank-two actions are distinct branches; their exact internal dispersion coefficients alone supply none of these attachments.

The finite classification and invariant-form receipts determine conditional algebraic shapes but do not construct this physical field/action package.

Gauge representation and hypercharge data do not by themselves derive these two global labels or prove their conservation.

Surviving rows are tested in the supplied epsilon-contraction and exterior-algebra grammar. The exhaustive finite result proves completeness only inside this declared grammar.

Without this attachment the census neither proves proton stability nor predicts a lifetime.

premises.name: time-indexed net evolution and time-slice generation interface
premises.statement: A source-selected time-indexed or Cauchy-region interface must be jointly realized with net-compatible evolution and a proof that its admitted slice algebra generates the corresponding evolved regional algebra. A supplied finite scalar action has an exact regional collar criterion and a common sheared Weyl net; this does not supply native continuous observable access, physical regions or a continuum time-slice realization. PR-43 supplies a flow on one full matrix block, PR-52 owns the physical time and causal reading, and the constructed Z/2 slot swap remains an internal finite symmetry. Continuous symmetry alone is neither necessary nor sufficient for the time-slice property.

premises.name: declared five-mode exterior component and mask-selection grammar
premises.statement: The bounded exterior-matter receipts supply the five-mode carrier V = C^3 + C^2 with trace-balanced integer charges q = 6Y = (-2, 3), omit exterior degrees zero and five, and use the ten remaining nontrivial isotypic rows with their committed color and weak dimensions, q6 column, exterior parity, and conjugation. The finite selection domain is exactly the 2^10 subsets of that table; admissibility requires nonemptiness, no row together with its conjugate, and vanishing of the displayed mixed gravitational-U(1), SU(3)^2 U(1), SU(2)^2 U(1), and U(1)^3 sums. This declared charged rank-fifteen exterior-table and mask grammar is distinct from the separately frozen PR-12 class, whose candidates have dimension at most twelve and zero abelian charges. Neither class contains the other. PR-59 neither source-selects physical matter nor proves completeness against other carriers, direct sums, vectorlike additions, neutral singlets, or light sectors.

premises.name: admissible scheduler class: mismatch non-increase clause
premises.statement: Every supported step of an admissible scheduler on the two-register repair carrier does not increase the declared defect mismatch, one unit per raised private defect flag. Typed as the mismatch_nonincrease clause of ObservableNormalForms.ProtectedObstructions.SchedulerClass.AdmissibleScheduler in Lean/ObservableNormalForms/ObservableNormalForms/SchedulerClassObstructions.lean; the all-scheduler defect cut consumes exactly this clause.

premises.name: admissible scheduler class: single-register locality clause
premises.statement: Every supported step writes at most one of the two registers, typed as the locality clause over the declared LocalMove grammar in Lean/ObservableNormalForms/ObservableNormalForms/SchedulerClassObstructions.lean. Declared; no obstruction theorem consumes it.

premises.name: admissible scheduler class: unit expected capacity clause
premises.statement: The expected declared capacity spend of every step, stepCost = privateCost + sharedCost integrated against the kernel row, is at most one unit, typed as the capacity_bound clause in Lean/ObservableNormalForms/ObservableNormalForms/SchedulerClassObstructions.lean. Declared; no obstruction theorem consumes it.

premises.name: two-register capacity-split reading
premises.statement: The first register of the committed two-bit repair carrier is read as the shared network-facing record and the second as the private local defect flag; privateCost charges one unit per private write and sharedCost one unit per shared write, and the self-update-only and network-update-only sub-classes are their zero-spend loci. The reading is a declaration, not a derivation.

premises.name: operational phase-instrument channel realization
premises.statement: A phase-sensitive measurement is represented by context- and outcome-indexed completely-positive trace-nonincreasing state-update maps whose sum in each context is trace preserving, whose induced effects agree with the declared effect table, and whose outcome readback agrees with the recorded public outcome. A matrix effect or exact Born table alone is not such an instrument.

premises.name: source-produced phase preparation and readback provenance
premises.statement: One source construction supplies the common preparation used across the phase and real contexts, selects the phase-sensitive effect or instrument, produces the public outcomes through that instrument, and binds preparation, context, operation, readback, and receipt custody to one run. Deterministic recomputation of Born weights from declared matrices does not supply this provenance.

premises.name: declared discrete kinetic term of the temporal Maxwell action
premises.statement: The temporal Maxwell packet is the Euler-Lagrange system of one declared discrete action on a finite step window: the committed local sourced face action at the forward step, with its committed seam-current coupling, plus the declared kinetic term (h/2)|E_n|^2 with E_n = -(A_{n+1}-A_n)/h - d phi_n, plus the port-load coupling h <rho_n, phi_n>. Stationarity under endpoint-vanishing variations of A is equivalent to the step-scaled Ampere update E_{n+1}-E_n = h (C^T B_{n+1} - J_n) at every interior step, and stationarity under variations of phi is equivalent to the Gauss constraint at every window step. The kinetic term and the step h are the declared inputs; the unit-step recurrence of the earlier packet is the h = 1 instance and is no separate declaration.

premises.name: declared finite one-doublet electroweak grammar
premises.statement: The finite electroweak composition uses one declared complex doublet with q=6Y equal to three, a four-parameter weak-hypercharge infinitesimal action with declared positive couplings, and the displayed finite normalization. This is a mathematical grammar declaration, not selection of a physical scalar field or kinetic action.

premises.name: declared finite quartic breaking packet
premises.statement: The finite composition declares lambda>0, a model-shell radius r>0, the potential lambda times (normSq(h)-r^2)^2, and the chosen point (0,r). Its minimizer, stabilizer, quadratic-coefficient, and gauge-mass-form identities are conditional finite consequences of this packet.

premises.name: declared finite Yukawa-line coefficient
premises.statement: The finite electroweak composition selects one epsilon-paired doublet-singlet Yukawa line with one declared real coefficient y and proves its exact bilinear value at the declared finite vacuum. It supplies no family matrices, physical chiral attachment, texture, phase, or measured mass identification.

premises.name: source homogeneous edge position action
premises.statement: The physical position action of the compared regime is homogeneous, its sole direct support is the complete thirty-direction edge orbit of the committed seam current, and its source weights are equal across the thirty directions. The committed corpus proves the control counterpart only: the seam-derived control symbol has complete edge support with one common squared chord and equal control weight (source_seam_edge30_control_certificate), and no committed theorem attaches that control symbol to a physical action.

premises.name: continuous field same-operator sector attachment
premises.statement: The compared observable lives in a continuous field sector, and the comparison reads the same operator sector that the committed source theorem fixes for the seam-derived symbol. No committed theorem selects the physical sector or identifies the committed symbol with a laboratory operator.

premises.name: cofinal gluing into the compared regime
premises.statement: The finite committed patch embeds cofinally into the compared regime, so that the committed edge-branch symbol governs propagation at the compared scales. No committed theorem supplies this gluing for the FZ-12 comparison path.

premises.name: declared finite carrier scale
premises.statement: One declared positive carrier scale fills the committed coefficient slot, giving C4 = -a^2/20, B0 = a^4/840, and B6 = -a^4/12600 at that scale. The committed manifold ratios are scale free and therefore do not select a value by themselves. This scoped non-forcing leaves independent source invariants such as a correlation length, refinement scale, defect density, or spectral gap as viable scale-selection routes.

premises.name: coherent frame and boost transport
premises.statement: One coherent frame carries the comparison, and a boost transport connects that frame to the source frame of the committed symbol, so that the intrinsic coefficients are read in a resolved frame. No committed theorem supplies frame resolution or boost transport for the FZ-12 comparison path.

premises.name: frozen nuisance and coverage readout rules
premises.statement: The readout of any eligible comparison isolates nuisance parameters and calibrates joint coverage under rules fixed before exposure, as the frozen decision rule requires for every verdict class. These are declared analysis conventions of the comparison protocol, not source-derivable structure.

premises.name: source-derived positive exclusivity lower bound
premises.statement: A pre-exposure same-action, same-sector source theorem fixes a positive lower bound a_min for the admissible scales in the comparison units, and the preregistered sensitivity and remainder contract covers every admissible scale at or above a_min. The frozen append-only clarification makes a null verdict conditional on exactly this obligation, owned by issue #664. No current source theorem supplies the bound. The permissive checklist realizes every positive label only because it stipulates the field; this proves no universal lower-bound no-go.

premises.name: pathwise weak fairness for canonical adaptive repair
premises.statement: Along one canonical adaptive repair run, every site that remains enabled throughout a tail is eventually selected on that tail. The premise is sufficient for the eventual constant record to be normal, but it is not needed for premise-free eventual constancy and is not derived or selected by canonical repair.

premises.name: work-conserving canonical adaptive choice
premises.statement: At every canonical adaptive repair state, whenever some site has an effective repair, the selected site has an effective repair. This stronger premise gives a normal and stable horizon bounded by the initial mismatch count. It is not required for premise-free eventual constancy or the weaker pathwise-fair normality theorem.

premises.name: bounded waste between canonical adaptive changes
premises.statement: From every scheduler index and every reducible canonical repair record, at least one genuine record change occurs among the next q+1 attempts for one declared natural q. The premise permits bounded equality stutter and yields a normal horizon no larger than (q+1) times the initial mismatch count. Canonical repair does not derive q or select a scheduler.

premises.name: sufficient cumulative attempt budget
premises.statement: The declared natural attempt budget B is at least (q+1) times the initial mismatch count for the same bounded-waste value q. Every scheduler invocation costs one unit, including equality stutter. This adequacy inequality supplies a finite execution capacity but no physical time, rate, energy, bandwidth, fee, or hardware interpretation.

premises.name: certified causal read support
premises.statement: Every semantic commit declares the register versions on which its enablement, accepted payload, visible label, or continuation genuinely depends, and the declared support is sound and complete for that dependence. The generated parent relation authenticates each cited version by requiring parent write-membership, the matching writer identifier, and value continuity from the parent's post-state to the child's pre-state. The Lean execution bridge threads states but does not infer support completeness from arbitrary executor code, and a repair that does not cite the injected seam version acquires no mismatch-response edge.

premises.name: abstract semantic ancestry acyclicity rank
premises.statement: An arbitrary inhabitant of the abstract SemanticEventLog certificate interface supplies a natural rank strictly increasing across every authenticated direct semantic parent edge as an acyclicity and well-foundedness witness. The canonical fresh, duplicate-free, carrier-complete executed-history constructor does not import this rank: it derives the witness from commit position and proves exact agreement with threaded authenticated provenance. The spacetime placement does not use these rank values; it computes canonical sourceHeight from authenticated parenthood. The supplied witness is not a repair schedule, modular parameter, clock reading, proper time, or global time coordinate; neither is sourceHeight.

premises.name: pathwise weak fairness for fixed node attempts
premises.statement: Along one attempt run of an input-independent fixed node federation, if one declared node remains failing throughout a tail, that exact node is eventually selected on the tail. The premise removes reducible equality-stutter tails but does not cause accepted-step termination, select a scheduler, bound attempts, or provide a physical rate.

premises.name: bounded waste between fixed node changes
premises.statement: From every scheduler index and every non-consensus state of one input-independent fixed node federation, at least one genuine state change occurs among the next q+1 attempts for one declared natural q. Combined with the source-specific triangular potential, the premise yields stable consensus within (q+1) times the triangular node bound. It is not implied by pathwise weak fairness and gives no physical rate or unit.

Derive accepted overlap holonomy and its projective implementer in the connected response group on the same histories, modulo the centralizer.

Supply an explicit map intertwining the candidate’s finite response with L/2 on this sector and verify it carries all three directions on the cell.

The paper also gives a quantitative route using ten timelike observers with matched bulk, area and stationarity errors o(ℓ⁴); it requires no separately assumed null-balance equation.

criteria.requires: Use a common vacuum and calibration. Establish that all admitted excitations couple to the same responsive geometry with one positive Newton constant.
criteria.note: The native scalar sector has no implemented universally coupled responsive geometry.

criteria.title: Null balance and tensor closure
criteria.requires: For the same source, state, tower and calibrated coupling, compare G(k,k) with 8πG times the measured T(k,k) on all nine spanning null design directions, control the residual, then apply independent Ward and geometric Bianchi identities to fix the remaining trace up to Λ.
criteria.note: No matched native curvature/stress experiment is present. The static radial counterexample in the spacetime paper belongs to a separately specified construction.

requirements.title: Clock dilation, three-dimensional fields, signal timing and bound-pair dynamics
requirements.purpose: Observers measure how a moving clock runs, whether a field varies along three independent spatial directions, and when a message can first be decoded. They also test whether separated loads form a lasting pair, where it travels and whether it returns, how its clock phase advances, and how its wave frequency depends on momentum.
requirements.reference: The archived positive and negative controls ran on an eight-slot periodic routing architecture. The historical numbers belong to that apparatus. The candidate columns use the current spherical law and state which preparations, sectors and services produced their records.

criteria.title: Time dilation of a moving clock
criteria.requires: Measure speed independently. Read a returning finite patch’s evolving hand and its rest companion at home. Reproduce the clock forecast and its tolerance on held journeys, clock constructions and speeds.
criteria.context: On the torus five long-wave moving/rest residuals were at most 0.00371 against a 0.035 limit. A broad packet missed by 0.06546. Two clocks agreed on five journeys. Six bound-clock flights passed the finite-packet correction.
criteria.note: A stationary ring has a measurable line against its reference. A transported clock, independent speed and fixed-home reunion remain open.

criteria.title: Three spatial directions in a field measured by observers
criteria.requires: Infer three independent directions and scales from timed patch records. Predict withheld field measurements across stations and refinements and test whether dropping any direction spoils them.
criteria.context: The torus supplied its three spatial routing axes. Nine stations predicted 120 held field values with RMS 0.001103. Omitting successive spatial derivatives raised RMS to 0.3123, 0.3246 and 0.3246. RER also recovered a three-dimensional Gram matrix from native cell records and, in a separate free-field inverse experiment, a supplied cube from eight relabelled channels.
criteria.note: The seam response BBᵀ has a three-dimensional first nonconstant eigenspace on one cell. The registered scalar generator supplies cell modes. A propagation experiment with independently surveyed stations remains open.

criteria.title: Earliest decodable message in observer time
criteria.requires: Choose a bit after setup. The receiver commits its answer by independently ranged early and late deadlines on its own patch clock. Test passive signals, every allowed relay and quiet controls. Record both accuracy and rare early clicks.
criteria.context: The torus passive receiver had early probability at most 5.878 × 10⁻³⁵, early balanced decoding at 50% and late decoding at 100%. An addressed relay decoded all 512 bits early. A pulse peak measures a different event from the first usable message.
criteria.note: The scalar service prepares and reads local pointer signals. Its protocol does not compare early and late remote decoding on observers’ clocks.

criteria.title: Formation of an enduring pair in an ordinary encounter
criteria.requires: Start with separated constituents. A patch records a birth and later an intact pair. Distinguish formation from binding after a measurement or deliberate preparation, report all quiet starts and compare disabled capture.
criteria.context: The archived simple routed encounter formed a pair with probability 1/2 and gave zero when its capture vertex was disabled. Preparation and capture rates depend on the experiment.
criteria.note: The pulse prepares the protected ring. The registered free scalar generator has no interaction term that binds two colliding objects. The separate conversion experiment changes the law.

criteria.title: Direction, coverage and return of a formed pair
criteria.requires: Register direction by the time order of local station records. Report intended and wrong-way crossings per enrolled start and per crossing for both launch senses. Read the marker and pair at return and include losses.
criteria.context: The archived late train reached 96.56% in the intended direction among crossings. Early coverage was 9.680% against 10% required. The closed-wire example had about 0.53% breakup after its marker’s second return.
criteria.note: The observed ring is exactly confined. The free scalar response has other modes, but the specified direction-and-return experiment has no registered formed-pair cohort.

criteria.title: Phase rate of a clock on the formed pair
criteria.requires: Read the same internal phase at several declared elapsed intervals using local reference records. Include visibility, rate uncertainty, source width, receiver aperture and quiet outcomes.
criteria.context: At width five the torus array reported 0.000439509–0.000440033 radians per home tick across six durations. The central layer failed. Widening the preparation from three to five changed the array rate by about 31%.
criteria.note: A pulsed cage gives 4.898982 and 4.898976 in local reference units under equal and unequal waits. A fuel read gives 4.898980. This is a stationary prepared cage with a supplied phase.

criteria.title: Relativistic matter-wave dispersion of the same formed object
criteria.requires: Independently measure rest frequency, signal speed and spatial phase gradient. Predict the moving object’s frequency in held directions and at multiple wavelengths with a changed-law control.
criteria.context: The archived routed pair passed 14 signed directions at periods 64, 128 and 256, with a 3.5% kinetic tolerance. Halving the spatial weight failed all 42 comparisons. The higher-momentum runs left the smooth regime.
criteria.note: The seam operator has the exact spectral relation ω² = m² + λ. Here λ comes from BBᵀ and m is supplied. The cage measures one internal gap. An observer-derived wavevector, independent signal speed and held moving-pair shell are open.

requirements.title: Patch clocks, stable excitations and a spacetime description
requirements.purpose: Record what the spherical candidates have already demonstrated at finite size and which ingredients a full spacetime reconstruction still needs.
requirements.reference: A patch can own one or several echosahedra and may share cells with another observer. Supplied references, detectors and local schedules belong to each experiment. A source comparison may use an unchanged reducing sector when the preparation, generator and readout coincide.

criteria.title: A fixed observer reads a material timing record
criteria.requires: A finite patch reads a local hand or periodic reference from physical registers at more than one setting. State how the source, cadence and readout are supplied.
criteria.context: This finite test credits a readable clock resource with its preparation and range. A universal clock rate or a shared screen-wide history is outside its scope.
criteria.note: A native cell’s ring detector and a prepared local reference yield a single phase line after a finite pulse. Stopping both cage modes removes the swing while its reference continues.

criteria.title: Own-history clock transport and fixed-home reunion
criteria.requires: A finite moving patch physically carries its hand, elapsed count and interval history. At reunion both owners recover the same home/traveller readings through a shared local register. State all supplied movement and gating services.
criteria.context: This measures local register custody and agreement at one event. A distribution over completed travel schedules also tests the closing filter over its declared finite capacity.
criteria.note: The cage phase can be read locally. It is fixed to the ring. The routed scratch service transports a control, with no moving cage hand or joint reunion record.

criteria.title: A prepared excitation persists and is locally detectable
criteria.requires: Give a fixed preparation, a patch readout, delays and a perturbation or interaction-off control. Demonstrate persistence of internal binding or protected local support and specify which is tested.
criteria.context: Later torus work added persistence as an eighth observation. Survival of a prepared state is independently testable and does not imply that the same state forms in a typical encounter.
criteria.note: The alternating four-seam ring and its partner span an invariant subspace. The detector reads the excitation over five waits. Altering the hopping breaks the line and its predicted records. Ring tests cover 20, 80 and 320 cells.

criteria.title: Propagation of a localized defect or bound excitation
criteria.requires: After a local excitation is identified, another local site or patch detects it with its identifying property intact. Specify whether transport is passive or serviced and keep disappearance and quiet outcomes.
criteria.context: Motion of a bound pair to another seam, transport of a registered load between patches and motion of a phase-carrying particle are distinct measurements. Only the first two meet this bounded location-change test.
criteria.note: The measured cage has exactly flat levels and remains confined to its ring. A separately named mobile-memory generator changes the dynamics. A mobile protected scalar excitation in the registered law remains open.

criteria.title: Smooth 3+1D description of a finite observer menu
criteria.requires: On the same candidate identify the recorded source, clock, positive angular form, radial propagation and refinement assumptions of the smooth-description proposition, or directly verify a declared family of held four-dimensional predictions with quantified errors.
criteria.context: RER’s smooth-effective-descriptions proposition proves approximation of every fixed finite admissible menu on bounded times by a free scalar on a smooth static 1+3 metric under S1 and S2 with radial Dirichlet interval. An earlier eight-channel free-field reconstruction inferred 12 cube edges and rank three, and predicted 16 withheld settings below 3 × 10⁻¹⁴ in probability. A separate 720-branch echosahedral experiment recovered a rank-three Gram matrix from repair records. In the separate OL-A1 fresh-seed signature replication the high-carrier arm recovered its threshold signature in 5/5 replicates and the lower arm in 2/5. The margin and ancestry controls failed. The small eigenvalue was about 3 × 10⁻⁵ relative to the largest and the robust signature lost a direction. The ledger keeps OL-A1 owed.
criteria.note: The free scalar law gives a native one-cell seam dispersion and a local phase reference. A source-to-metric map with radial propagation and clocked refinements over this law’s observer records remains open.

criteria.title: Three independent spatial response components in local patch records
criteria.requires: Infer the multiplicity and Gram matrix of the slowest nonconstant response from records of an observer with a finite spatial aperture. Predict new local readouts and bound the loss from a two-component description.
criteria.context: The source supplies one native cell, sharp preparations, complete local detectors, the weak-exposure branch and relative dwell settings. The inverse receives relabelled probabilities and a uniform-hopping model class. It receives no coordinates, spatial dimension, seams or Hamiltonian. The measurement concerns the local angular response. OBS-02 asks whether three directions propagate between observers.
criteria.note: The unsigned seam–port incidence sends the same rank-three projector into the actual scalar squared-frequency response. A detector-table reconstruction of that rank on physical scalar preparations remains open.

criteria.title: Three spatial response components reach neighbouring patches
criteria.requires: Use native evolution to transmit independently prepared components from one sender to real neighbouring patches. Decode held combinations from local port/quiet counts, test rank-two and sham controls, and check predictions at untrained stations or exposure times.
criteria.context: This section tests the transfer of prepared local load-probability contrasts on a one-load source. The exposures are externally set. The three receivers contribute separate local inboxes.
criteria.note: The scalar sector uses different registers and propagation. This receiver experiment has no scalar-channel counterpart.

criteria.title: Two kinds of material hand agree on the same accepted repair events
criteria.requires: Compare a transported oscillator with a registered event hand on the same guided journeys and local accepted repair histories. Use independent phase readout, a frozen equivalence margin, rest calibration and a distinct raw-event control.
criteria.context: The accepted-event oscillator and event hand implement distinct transducers of a common tick stream. The alternative oscillator counts every positive primary. Their comparison isolates the physical event selection.
criteria.note: The stationary cage line has no corresponding guided two-hand replication.

criteria.title: Optically ranged reunion on held native links and motion schedules
criteria.requires: A finite home patch measures a reciprocal light time, receives a physical arrival report and reads both elapsed words at reunion. Compare the optical forecast with the material hand for prospectively held schedules on different native links. Require all in-domain tests to meet their frozen uncertainty band, and report overflow and raw-event controls separately.
criteria.context: The relative pace of the reciprocal light guide and transfer opportunities is provided. Physical link installations with identical service timelines share their statistical cohort.
criteria.note: A held reciprocal optical comparison of the transported scalar oscillator is open.

requirements.purpose: Assess the 31 OpenWave physical targets on each of the three RER candidate laws. The criterion number follows upstream row order. A partial entry names the finite measurement and the missing step to the physical target. These local assessments are independent of the upstream M10 column, which evaluates a different candidate.

criteria.note: Electric topological charge and a forbidden splitting channel have yet to be identified.

criteria.title: Electron rest energy (mass)
criteria.requires: Select a localized state dynamically. With its energy anchored at 511 keV, predict and independently measure another physical quantity fixed by that anchor.
criteria.note: A prepared four-seam branch has a measured single-addition gap. Two separated additions give the sum in joint phase records. The 511 keV anchor alone supplies a scale. An independent electron observable and identification remain open.

criteria.requires: Measure an internally initiated, frequency-rigid oscillation whose angular frequency equals the measured rest energy divided by ℏ.
criteria.note: After a finite preparation pulse two local clocks resolve a free line at about 4.89898, agreeing with a separate fuel-gap measurement. Autonomous onset and the electron rest-energy identification remain open.

criteria.title: Particle stability (Derrick escape)
criteria.requires: Demonstrate free persistence of the candidate particle in the electron sector, including its localized preparation and readout.
criteria.note: Free persistence succeeds for a prepared four-seam excitation. The exact invariant subspace keeps its support localized at every free time and the local fuel records test its return. The electron assignment remains open.

criteria.title: Magnetic moment μ (g ≈ 2, magnetostatics)
criteria.requires: Measure a static magnetic dipole sourced by internal circulation in the stationary electron, its gyromagnetic factor near two and its Larmor response.
criteria.note: The electron dipole, gyromagnetic factor and field-driven precession require an electromagnetic readout.

criteria.title: Angular momentum J (spin ℏ/2)
criteria.requires: Measure angular momentum of magnitude ℏ/2 carried by the field of the same electron state.
criteria.note: Field angular momentum has yet to be measured on an identified electron.

criteria.title: Spin-½ statistics (720° double cover)
criteria.requires: Interfere a full rotation, or a two-core exchange, with a reference and recover a minus sign. A dynamically selected half-turn discriminated from a polar control provides intermediate evidence.
criteria.note: The scalar register construction uses fermionic operators. An interference measurement of a dynamically selected two-core exchange or 2π rotation remains open.

criteria.title: Antimatter + annihilation
criteria.requires: Observe a particle and its conjugate convert into radiation. Resolve the two- and three-photon positronium channels as follow-up measurements.
criteria.note: Local instruments distinguish adding and removing an object from the filled reference. The sharp cage occupations persist during free evolution. A radiative annihilation channel requires different evidence.

criteria.title: Neutrinos (neutral states)
criteria.requires: Identify electrically neutral, light excitations among the products of a decay.
criteria.note: The scalar law supports neutral excitations relative to its supplied gauge reference. A light neutral product released in a weak decay remains unidentified.

criteria.title: Neutrino oscillations (PMNS)
criteria.requires: Distinguish three neutrino flavours through production and detection, observe their oscillations and extract the PMNS angles.
criteria.note: The resolved bands belong to one scalar channel. Three flavour-labelled channels, their oscillations and mixing angles remain open.

criteria.title: Lepton mass spectrum (μ, τ)
criteria.requires: Resolve precisely three charged-lepton minima and compare their relative masses with 1, 207 and 3477.
criteria.note: Several scalar lines have measured frequencies for a supplied level parameter. A charged-lepton family assignment and three mass ratios remain open.

criteria.title: Quarks
criteria.requires: Recover fractional electric charge from a partial winding of a quark string.
criteria.note: An electric response tied to fractional string winding remains unmeasured.

criteria.title: Baryons: bound state (p, n)
criteria.requires: Recover a persistent bound composite whose three constituents are identified as quarks.
criteria.note: A three-quark identification remains open.

criteria.title: Baryons: mass ordering + charge profile
criteria.requires: Distinguish neutron and proton, obtain a heavier neutron and resolve the positive-core and negative-shell charge distribution.
criteria.note: The neutron and proton identities, mass order and resolved electric profile remain open.

criteria.title: Baryons: exact masses
criteria.requires: Predict the proton and neutron rest energies from the field and compare with 938.3 and 939.6 MeV, respectively.
criteria.note: A common field-based prediction for both identified baryon energies remains open.

criteria.title: Deuteron (binding + quadrupole)
criteria.requires: Demonstrate deuteron binding below the sum of the proton and neutron masses and measure its electric quadrupole.
criteria.note: No deuteron binding and electric quadrupole measurement exists on the identified constituents.

criteria.title: Nuclear structure (levels, halos)
criteria.requires: Recover nuclear binding across species, excitation levels and lifetimes of halo nuclei.
criteria.note: Identified nuclear species with binding, spectroscopy and halo lifetime records remain open.

criteria.title: Mesons (π, K)
criteria.requires: Identify pion and kaon states and a strange decay such as Λ⁰ → p + π⁻.
criteria.note: Meson assignments and a decay tagged by strangeness remain open.

criteria.title: Dark matter candidate
criteria.requires: Demonstrate a stable massive excitation with measured neutrality as a dark-matter candidate.
criteria.note: The prepared four-seam state is persistent. Its dark-matter identification requires electric neutrality and a moving inertial-mass measurement on the same branch.

criteria.title: Electric force (Coulomb 1/r, electrostatics)
criteria.requires: Measure an inverse-distance far-field potential sourced by one elementary electric charge. A strength claim also needs α derived from the mechanism.
criteria.note: The elementary free scalar law is quadratic. Green kernels of the seam operator alone establish no charged far-field potential measured by a unit source and a test object.

criteria.title: Lorentz covariance (+ Coulomb = EM)
criteria.requires: Establish Lorentz covariance without a preferred inertial frame, including contraction of boosted states and an operational signal-speed bound.
criteria.note: Four one-cell wave bands follow a relativistic scalar dispersion. The continuous-duration equal-term test has influence at arbitrarily early times. Native boosts, contraction and a finite operational signal-speed bound on the sphere remain open.

criteria.title: Strong force: confinement
criteria.requires: Measure a linear confining potential between identified colour charges and recover a string tension near 1 GeV/fm.
criteria.note: A colour-source separation scan and a measured confining tension remain open.

criteria.title: Running coupling
criteria.requires: Resolve a coupling that changes with measurement scale, including the onset near the physical core radius.
criteria.note: A scale scan of a physical coupling referred to the same core radius remains open.

criteria.title: Weak force: muon decay
criteria.requires: Observe an identified muon decay into an electron with neutral products.
criteria.note: Muon, electron and neutral decay-product records remain open.

criteria.title: Weak force: beta decay (n → p)
criteria.requires: Resolve neutron decay into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino, and measure parity violation.
criteria.note: A tagged beta decay and its parity asymmetry remain open.

criteria.title: Gravity: Newton limit (GEM)
criteria.requires: Recover an attractive inverse-square force between masses from the gravitoelectromagnetic limit. Credit for the strength requires G to follow from the mechanism.
criteria.note: A sourced gravitoelectromagnetic force law and its strength remain unmeasured.

criteria.title: Gravity: local metric phenomena
criteria.requires: Measure local curved-metric phenomena with material clocks and light, such as bending, gravitational redshift or Shapiro delay.
criteria.note: A sourced gravitational field with independent clock or light propagation records remains open.

criteria.title: Cosmology: Λ / cosmic acceleration
criteria.requires: Obtain a cosmological constant that explains acceleration from the model dynamics, identify outstanding gaps and give a falsification test.
criteria.note: A derived cosmological constant, acceleration observable and falsification test remain open.

criteria.title: EM waves (Maxwell)
criteria.requires: Recover Maxwell dynamics and measure transverse electromagnetic disturbances travelling at the limiting speed.
criteria.note: The exports distinguish gapped propagating seam modes and a gapless scalar branch. The measured modes have yet to furnish Maxwell dynamics and a transverse electromagnetic signal at a common speed.

criteria.title: Quantum wave equation (Klein-Gordon)
criteria.requires: Recover the Klein–Gordon energy–momentum relation for propagating matter using independently identifiable spatial and temporal observables.
criteria.note: The measured one-cell scalar bands agree with the square of the first-order seam operator, ω² = m² + λ. A multi-cell matter wave with independently reconstructed physical momentum and the third spatial direction remains open.

criteria.title: Orbital quantization (atomic structure)
criteria.requires: Observe standing-wave bound levels with a hydrogen-like spectrum, including characteristic spacings.
criteria.note: Free scalar excitations have discrete cage levels. The quadratic matter sector supplies no hydrogen-like bound spectrum around another excitation.

requirements.title: Standard Model particle identifications
requirements.purpose: Identify all 17 elementary particle types on one frozen candidate. Each species has a local preparation or production channel, reproducible detection statistics, and a dictionary that distinguishes its nearest alternatives. A declaration of a field or an input mass cannot identify the excitation.
requirements.reference: Count six quark flavours, three charged leptons, three active neutrino flavour channels, four gauge-boson types and the Higgs. W covers both signs, and the gluon entry covers the eight colour components. Resolve conjugate partners where distinct. Neutrino flavour is defined by weak production and detection; its propagation can mix mass eigenstates. Composite hadrons provide evidence for confined quarks and gluons. A graviton and a sterile neutrino are outside this inventory.

criteria.title: Up
criteria.requires: Recover the spin-half colour-triplet sector, its electric and weak responses, and a flavour discriminator in colour-singlet production, decay or scattering records. Resolve the conjugate sector. Light up-type flavour, charge +2/3.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Down
criteria.requires: Recover the spin-half colour-triplet sector, its electric and weak responses, and a flavour discriminator in colour-singlet production, decay or scattering records. Resolve the conjugate sector. Light down-type flavour, charge −1/3.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Strange
criteria.requires: Recover the spin-half colour-triplet sector, its electric and weak responses, and a flavour discriminator in colour-singlet production, decay or scattering records. Resolve the conjugate sector. Distinguish strangeness from light down flavour.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Charm
criteria.requires: Recover the spin-half colour-triplet sector, its electric and weak responses, and a flavour discriminator in colour-singlet production, decay or scattering records. Resolve the conjugate sector. Identify charm production or weak transitions separately from up.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Bottom
criteria.requires: Recover the spin-half colour-triplet sector, its electric and weak responses, and a flavour discriminator in colour-singlet production, decay or scattering records. Resolve the conjugate sector. Resolve bottom-flavoured production and decay.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Top
criteria.requires: Recover the spin-half colour-triplet sector, its electric and weak responses, and a flavour discriminator in colour-singlet production, decay or scattering records. Resolve the conjugate sector. Resolve the heavy up-type resonance and its weak decay.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Electron
criteria.requires: Resolve spin half, unit negative charge, colour neutrality and weak interactions. Discriminate the three generations and their positive-charge conjugates through spectral or decay measurements. Light stable charged-lepton branch.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Muon
criteria.requires: Resolve spin half, unit negative charge, colour neutrality and weak interactions. Discriminate the three generations and their positive-charge conjugates through spectral or decay measurements. Distinct mass and leptonic decay channel.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Tau
criteria.requires: Resolve spin half, unit negative charge, colour neutrality and weak interactions. Discriminate the three generations and their positive-charge conjugates through spectral or decay measurements. Third charged-lepton branch, with its weak decay channels.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Electron neutrino
criteria.requires: Resolve a neutral spin-half weak sector, tag flavour by the accompanying charged lepton, and relate production, propagation and detection with the same mixing dictionary. Distinguish neutrino and antineutrino interaction channels where measurable. Electron-tagged weak current.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Muon neutrino
criteria.requires: Resolve a neutral spin-half weak sector, tag flavour by the accompanying charged lepton, and relate production, propagation and detection with the same mixing dictionary. Distinguish neutrino and antineutrino interaction channels where measurable. Muon-tagged weak current.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Tau neutrino
criteria.requires: Resolve a neutral spin-half weak sector, tag flavour by the accompanying charged lepton, and relate production, propagation and detection with the same mixing dictionary. Distinguish neutrino and antineutrino interaction channels where measurable. Tau-tagged weak current.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Photon
criteria.requires: Identify polarization, charge and the current coupled to the same propagating vector excitation. Massless transverse electromagnetic response and its coupling to the measured electric current.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Gluon
criteria.requires: Identify polarization, charge and the current coupled to the same propagating vector excitation. Colour-octet strong-current response and non-Abelian couplings in gauge-invariant signals.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: W boson
criteria.requires: Identify polarization, charge and the current coupled to the same propagating vector excitation. Both signs of the massive charged weak vector and charged-current transitions.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Z boson
criteria.requires: Identify polarization, charge and the current coupled to the same propagating vector excitation. Massive neutral weak vector, its polarizations and neutral-current couplings.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.

criteria.title: Higgs boson
criteria.requires: Identify a neutral spin-zero resonance with independently distinguished couplings in the same electroweak sector. Electroweak symmetry-breaking scalar and its characteristic production or decay responses.
criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.
